children: Nabors reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $872.2 million, up 7% sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA of $245.5 million. Net loss attributable to Nabors shareholders was $11.2 million, while adjusted free cash flow was $74.5 million. The company expects full-year adjusted EBITDA of approximately $930 million and adjusted free cash flow of $100 million to $110 million.
Operating revenue was $872.2 million, up from $814.8 million in the prior quarter and $818.2 million in the year-ago quarter.
Adjusted EBITDA was $245.5 million, compared with $221.7 million in the second quarter and $236.3 million a year earlier.
Adjusted operating income was $85.8 million, versus $61.1 million in the prior quarter and $76.0 million in the year-ago quarter.
Net loss attributable to Nabors shareholders was $11.2 million; consolidated net income was $16.0 million.
Adjusted diluted loss per share was $1.24. Adjusted free cash flow was $74.5 million, up from $12.3 million in the second quarter.
Average total rigs working reached 177.1, up from 171.2 in the second quarter. The Lower 48 average working fleet increased to 72.8 rigs from 67.8.
SANAD deployed its 17th newbuild rig in Saudi Arabia. One more rig is scheduled for deployment in 2026 and two in the first quarter of 2027, completing the planned 20-rig newbuild fleet.
Nabors signed a multiyear contract for one rig in Venezuela, with operations expected to begin in early 2027 and marking its return to the country.
Lower 48 rigs set drilling records for customers in North Dakota and South Texas. Canrig also secured commitments for four more RZR rig floor automation modules, bringing planned deployments to six.
